data.title: MINILUXE REPORTS THIRD QUARTER AND YEAR-TO-DATE FINANCIAL RESULTS FOR THE 13 AND 39 WEEKS ENDED SEPTEMBER 27, 2026
data.description:
Net Revenue Up 6% in the Third Quarter; System Sales Exceed $8M in a Quarter; Company Makes Multiple Growth Investments in Q3, Including New Studio Opening and Acquisition

All reported figures in U.S. Dollars unless otherwise noted

Boston, MA, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- MiniLuxe Holding Corp. today announced its financial results for the 13 weeks and 39 weeks ended September 27, 2026 (“Q3 2026” and “YTD 2026”, respectively). The comparative prior year periods are the 13 weeks and 39 weeks ended September 28, 2025.

MiniLuxe is on a mission to make self-care something you can feel good about, starting with your nails. The Company delivers premium nail care in studios known for hospital-grade hygiene, cleaner polishes, and treatments that are better for you and for the people who provide them. What sets MiniLuxe apart is its people and culture, which are at the center of its competitive advantage. In an industry infamous for churn and poor working conditions, MiniLuxe has retained 86% of its hourly workforce on average over each of the last three years. Team members who are with the Company five years or more receive stock options, giving them a stake in the Company’s success, along with real career paths. Today, more than half of MiniLuxe’s service professionals (nail designers and waxing specialists) have reached that milestone.

The third quarter of 2026 delivered another quarter of year-over-year growth, with total Company net revenue up 6.1% to $7.7M and system sales up 8% to $8.1M from $7.5M in Q3 2025. Growth was driven by continued same-studio sales gains in both volume and mix. System sales include sales from all MiniLuxe studios, including franchised locations. The quarter extends a long, unbroken run of year-over-year revenue growth, reflecting continued demand for MiniLuxe services.

The Company made multiple growth investments in the third quarter: new studios, new AI-driven, geo-targeted paid marketing tests, upgrades to existing studios, and additional nail designer hours ahead of the fourth-quarter holiday season, its period of peak demand. While these initiatives resulted in some short-term margin pullback, management expects them to deliver meaningful returns over the longer term. After the quarter ended, the Company also put in place its first price increase in approximately three years, of approximately 5%, which management expects to more than offset rising labor and health care benefit costs.

  • New studios: The Company opened its Mansfield, Massachusetts joint-venture studio on July 30 and acquired a majority interest in an existing studio in Burlington, Massachusetts on September 4. The third quarter was also the first full quarter for the new MiniLuxe Lakewood studio in Dallas.
  • Marketing tests: Early results are encouraging, with some test studios attracting record numbers of new clients who are also returning faster for repeat visits.
  • Studio upgrades: The Company began renovating several existing studios with new dual stations that allow a manicure and pedicure at the same time. In the first studios, these stations cost at least 50% less than legacy stations, and productivity per station has been as much as double that of legacy pedicure stations.
  • Nail designer hours: Staffed hours were up 7% over the prior year, which positions the Company well for fourth-quarter demand.

MiniLuxe’s Focus and Key Strategic Pillars in Q3 2026

The Company continued to make meaningful progress across each of its core strategic pillars in the third quarter of fiscal 2026:

  • Attract, develop and retain high-quality nail designer talent;
  • Drive growth through operating partners and franchise partners;
  • Accelerate overall studio-level profitability and drive overall Company profitability;
  • Strengthen balance sheet with sufficient capital to execute against growth plans.

Highlights of Business Performance

  • Total Company net revenue grew 6.1% to $7.7M in Q3 2026 from $7.3M in Q3 2025, bringing year-to-date revenue to $21.8M, up 4.3% from $20.9M in YTD 2025.

As a percentage of net revenue, G&A was flat year over year at approximately 49.6%. Year to date, G&A was $11.10M versus $10.90M in YTD 2025, up 1.9%, and declined to 51.0% of net revenue from 52.2%.

Most of the change was driven by the timing of expenses and one-time items. Excluding one-time items, management estimates Normalized Adjusted EBITDA of ($1.27M) in the quarter, compared with ($1.02M) in Q3 2025.
  • During the third quarter, the Company issued 1,428,571 Class A Subordinate Voting Shares at a deemed price of $0.35 per share in settlement of a $500,000 third-party obligation (the gift-card holdback from the Paintbox acquisition).
  • At the end of Q3 2026 (September 27, 2026), cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash were $4.5M (Q2 2026: $6.1M; year-end 2025: $4.5M), and working capital was positive at $0.2M.

The Company continued to expand through operating partners and franchise partners. Overall gross franchise sales were up 53% in the third quarter and 102% year to date. The Mansfield, Massachusetts joint-venture studio opened on July 30, 2026, the Lakewood (Dallas) studio reopened as a MiniLuxe studio on June 5, 2026, and the Burlington, Massachusetts studio, acquired September 4, 2026, is operated through a 51%-owned limited liability company with its existing owner as operating partner.

Management Commentary

“In Q3, we continued to grow revenue year over year and expanded our studio footprint, with new studio openings and new locations in development. We also increased total nail designer hours and put marketing tests in place to attract new customers. We are already seeing early results as we attract new customers and see repeat visits, and we believe these investments will deliver a significant return over the medium to longer term. One of the most noteworthy statistics for me is that about half of our customer base is now Gen Z, which bodes well for the longevity of our brand and customer lifetime value.” – Tony Tjan, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

Other Developments

  • Substantial Issuer Bid (SIB). The Company’s SIB for up to C$6.0 million of its Class A Subordinate Voting Shares expired at 5:00 p.m. (Toronto time) on September 24, 2026. No Subordinate Voting Shares were purchased under the offer and all tendered shares were returned to shareholders.
  • Paintbox New York studio. On September 7, 2026, the Company closed its “store-in-store” Paintbox studio in New York, New York. The Company had a short-term arrangement with a hair studio to use its space as a “store-in-store” concept, and the arrangement was not extended.
  • Acquisition of Belle Vista Nail Studio. On September 4, 2026, the Company formed MNLX Burlington JV LLC and acquired the assets of Belle Vista Nail Studio in Burlington, Massachusetts for cash consideration of approximately $0.3M, issuing a 49% interest in the new company to the sellers. MiniLuxe will convert this studio to its own brand in 2027.

The Company continues to evaluate accretive M&A opportunities and is in discussions with several nail studio operators that it believes fit its purpose of empowering nail designers, and where it can create shared value by applying MiniLuxe’s brand standards and back-office infrastructure.

Non-IFRS Measures and Reconciliation of Non-IFRS Measures

This press release references certain non-IFRS measures used by management. These measures are not recognized under International Financial Reporting Standards (“IFRS”), do not have a standardized meaning prescribed by IFRS, and are therefore unlikely to be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. Rather, these measures are provided as additional information to complement those IFRS measures by providing further understanding of the Company’s results of operations from management’s perspective. Accordingly, these measures should not be considered in isolation nor as a substitute for analysis of the Company’s financial information reported under IFRS. The non-IFRS measures referred to in this press release are “Adjusted EBITDA”, “Normalized Adjusted EBITDA”, and system sales.

Adjusted EBITDA

Management believes Adjusted EBITDA most accurately reflects the commercial reality of the Company’s operations on an ongoing basis by adding back non-cash expenses. Additionally, the rent-related adjustments ensure that studio-related expenses align with revenue generated over the corresponding time periods.

Adjusted EBITDA is calculated by adding back fixed asset depreciation, right-of-use asset amortization under IFRS 16, asset disposal, and share-based compensation expense to IFRS operating income, then deducting cash rent expenses net of lease abatements. When relevant, we will add back adjustments made to the P&L as a result of accounting policies that are non-cash or do not have operational impacts (for example, inventory adjustments or deferred revenue). IFRS operating income is revenue less cost of sales (gross profit), additionally adjusted for general and administrative expenses, and depreciation and amortization expenses. Normalized Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as Adjusted EBITDA, further adjusted to (i) remove items that management considers one-time or not representative of ongoing operations, and (ii) present the comparative period on a basis consistent with the current period. Management uses Normalized Adjusted EBITDA to assess the Company’s run-rate operating performance. It should be read together with, and not as a substitute for, operating loss and Adjusted EBITDA.

About MiniLuxe

MiniLuxe Holding Corp. is a Boston-based lifestyle brand and talent empowerment platform transforming the fragmented beauty and self-care industry through its premium service brand, proprietary products, and operating platform. For more than 15 years, MiniLuxe has delivered high-quality nail care, waxing, and esthetic services through a growing network of company-owned, joint venture, and partner-operated studios, completing more than 5 million services to date.

The Company is recognized for its elevated service experience, rigorous hygiene standards, non-toxic products, modern studio design, and commitment to socially responsible labor practices. MiniLuxe’s differentiated model is designed to create better outcomes for both clients and beauty professionals through career development, economic mobility, equity participation, and future ownership opportunities.

MiniLuxe is expanding its reach through a multi-pronged growth strategy that includes new studio development, franchising, and the acquisition and conversion of existing nail studios. By combining a trusted consumer brand, proprietary products, operating expertise, and technology-enabled systems, the Company offers entrepreneurs and operators the opportunity to partner with a proven platform while preserving a strong focus on talent development and service excellence.

Through its growing studio network and product portfolio, MiniLuxe seeks to build the leading trusted brand in beauty and self-care while generating long-term value for clients, talent, and shareholders.

data.title: Bradesco's Trabuco accepts invitation to be Brazil's finance minister, source says
data.description:
By Lisandra Paraguassu and Paula Laier

Lender Bradesco's chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco has accepted President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's invitation to be Brazil's next finance minister, a person close to the matter told Reuters on Thursday.

Reuters earlier reported, citing two people with knowledge of the negotiations, that Lula had already approached Trabuco about taking over the finance ministry. The banker has had a close relationship with the president for many years.

Trabuco and Lula are expected to meet in Brasilia later on Thursday. Local magazine Veja first reported the news that the Bradesco chairman had accepted the role.

Approached by Reuters, neither Bradesco nor the presidency responded to requests for comment.

Brazil's financial markets have deteriorated since Lula beat right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro in October's presidential election, with the country's real currency depreciating against the dollar, pushing Lula to sound out a market-friendly figure for the finance ministry to ease investors' fears.

As rumors of the approach to Trabuco started circulating on Wednesday, markets responded positively, with the real (BRL) gaining ground while the Brazilian stock market's benchmark index rose by 6% on Thursday.

Lula is expected to announce a first group of ministers for his new government next week after he returns from the Mercosur summit in Montevideo, Uruguay.

Other names initially considered for the finance ministry were Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, who reportedly told allies he would like the post, and Rafael Fonteles, who was re-elected governor of Piaui state.

SIR's Fiscal 2026 year consisted of 52 weeks compared to 53 weeks for Fiscal 2025, and the Company's Q4 2026 consisted of 16 weeks compared to 17 weeks for the fourth quarter of Fiscal 2025. Therefore, all financial information provided in this news release for the fourth quarter of Fiscal 2025 and for Fiscal 2025, unless otherwise noted, includes an additional week of operations that should be considered when comparing to the current year periods.

  • Food and beverage revenue from corporate restaurant operations increased by 3.3% to $103.7 million, compared to $100.4 million for the 17-week period ended August 31, 2025 ("Q4 2025").
  • Consolidated Same Store Sales ("SSS") (1) decreased by 1.6%. If the additional week of revenue, as described above, was removed from Q4 2025, consolidated SSS(1) for Q4 2026 increased by 4.9%.

The positive variances in Q4 2026 compared to Q4 2025 and Fiscal 2026 compared to Fiscal 2025 primarily reflected the change in the amortized cost of the Ordinary LP Units and Class A Units of the SIR Royalty Limited Partnership (the "Partnership") that SIR holds, lower interest costs and increased earnings from restaurant operations, partially offset by increased cost of corporate restaurant operations.

The slight decrease was primarily attributable to an increase in cost of corporate restaurant operations, partially offset by an increase in revenue from corporate restaurant operations and decreases in corporate costs and interest expense. Adjusted Net Earnings(2) were $9.9 million in Fiscal 2026, compared to $9.8 million in Fiscal 2025. The increase is primarily attributable to an increase in revenue from corporate restaurant operations and a decrease in interest expense, partially offset by increases in cost of corporate restaurant operations, corporate costs and other expenses.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

As at August 30, 2026, SIR had cash (net of the cash balance of the Partnership) of $8.4 million compared to $12.5 million as at August 31, 2025, and had drawn approximately $37.7 million against the $68.0 million maximum principal borrowing amount under the Company's credit facilities.

Outlook

SIR continues to monitor consumer spending behavior in light of current evolving macroeconomic factors, including inflation, interest rates and the impact of cross-border tariffs between Canada and the United States, and their potential impact on the Canadian economy and consumer confidence. Ongoing business impacts due to changes in the minimum wage and rising commodity costs have been influential in the bar and restaurant industry's changes in pricing overall.

SIR continues to innovate and provide immersive new product and service offerings to increase dine-in guest visits and to capitalize on the growth of take-out and delivery services in commercial foodservice.

The Jack Astor's + Freida's location in Oshawa, Ontario, and three new Scaddabush locations in Aurora, Windsor and Kanata, Ontario are expected to be added to the Royalty Pooled Restaurants effective January 1, 2027.

SIR has leased two properties – in London, Ontario and Dartmouth, Nova Scotia – upon which it plans to develop two new Scaddabush locations. SIR has also leased a property in Windsor, Ontario upon which it plans to develop a new Jack Astor's + Freida's location. There can be no assurance at this time that these planned new restaurants will be opened, or that any of these five new locations will become part of the Royalty Pooled Restaurants.

SIR is pursuing additional sites to continue the successful growth of its Scaddabush and Jack Astor's + Freida's concepts. SIR will also continue its practice of investing in existing restaurants to drive improved sales and earnings. In consideration of the ongoing economic and market conditions mentioned above, restaurant opening and renovation plans will be reviewed regularly and adjusted as necessary.

TORONTO, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Mitchell Cohen, Chief Executive Officer and President of Urbanfund Corp. (TSX-V: UFC) (“Urbanfund” or the “Company”), confirmed today that the Company has filed its financial statements for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 (the “Consolidated Financial Statements”) and corresponding Management’s Discussion and Analysis (“MD&A”).

BUSINESS OVERVIEW AND STRATEGY

Business Overview

Urbanfund Corp. is an incorporated entity listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (“TSX-V”) under the symbol UFC. The Company is a reporting issuer in Alberta, British Columbia and Ontario. Urbanfund’s focus is to invest in Canadian real estate and real estate related projects with a focus on a mix of both residential and commercial properties. The Company’s assets are located in Toronto, Richmond Hill, Markham, Vaughan, Belleville, Kitchener and London, Ontario, Quebec City and Montreal, Quebec and Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.

Operational Highlights

Part of Urbanfund’s strength is its ability to attract partners with proven track records with both residential and commercial development expertise. Urbanfund continues to build alliances with its strategic partners:

  • Kolt 135 East Beaver Creek LP (“Creek LP”) – In August 2026, Urbanfund invested $1,575,000 in Creek LP representing a 50% limited partnership interest. Creek LP owns an industrial complex comprising nine units with a total area of 28,506 square feet, located at 135 East Beaver Creek Road, Richmond Hill, Ontario. The partnership intends to renovate, change to condominium title and sell units in the complex.
  • Kolt 30 Freshway LP (“Freshway LP”) - In August 2026, Urbanfund invested $1,668,258 in Freshway LP representing a 41.52% limited partnership interest. Freshway LP owns an industrial complex comprising three buildings with 27 units for a total area of 41,034 square feet, located at 30 Freshway Drive, Vaughan, Ontario. The partnership intends to renovate, change to condominium title and sell units in the complex.
  • 270-330 Esna Park Drive, Markham - During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, nine commercial units were sold for sales proceeds of $1,999,913 (September 30, 2025 – 18 commercial units for $3,354,897). To date, the Company’s capital contribution of $1,660,000 has been fully returned, and an additional profit of $1,049,775 has been received.
  • 1040 Martin Grove Road, Toronto - During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, three commercial units were sold for sales proceeds of $1,163,947 (September 30, 2025 – four commercial units for $1,685,124). To date, the Company’s capital contribution of $1,870,000 has been fully returned, and an additional profit distribution of $822,545 has been received.
  • 67-69 Westmore Drive, Etobicoke – During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the final two commercial units were sold for total sales proceeds of $1,372,000 (September 30, 2025 – four commercial units for $2,257,660). To date, the Company’s capital contribution of $3,120,000 has been fully returned, and an additional profit distribution of $5,053,399 has been received.
  • 3080-3094 Don Mills Road & 200 Van Horne Avenue, Toronto – On December 1, 2025, the Company completed the refinancing of its property, securing a new facility of $16,293,116 at a fixed interest rate of 3.55% for a five-year term. The proceeds were used to fully repay the existing mortgage of $8,022,140 on the property, with the remaining funds available to support general corporate purposes and future growth initiatives, as determined by the Board.

DIVIDEND REINVESTMENT PLAN (“DRIP”)

On June 17, 2015, the Company adopted a dividend policy (the “Dividend Policy”) and implemented dividend reinvestment plans for the Company’s common and preferred shareholders (collectively, the “DRIP”). The DRIP is a voluntary program permitting holders of our common and preferred shares to automatically, and without charge, reinvest quarterly dividends to acquire additional common shares at a discount to the volume-weighted average market price as of the date of payment.

On June 22, 2021, Urbanfund amended its Dividend Policy to increase the annual dividend rate to $0.05 per common share and $0.05 per Series A preferred share, or 67% increase from the previous year, payable quarterly in the amount of $0.0125 per common share and Series A preferred share.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Urbanfund issued 149,246 common shares valued at $125,862 to participants enrolled in the DRIP (September 30, 2025 – 153,894 and $119,038). The average participation rate of the DRIP was 6.32% (September 30, 2025 – 5.99%).

NON-IFRS MEASURES

In addition to reported IFRS measures, industry practice is to evaluate real estate entities giving consideration to certain non-IFRS performance measures such as funds from operations, adjusted cash flows from operations and net operating income. Management believes that these measures are helpful to investors because they are widely recognized measures of Urbanfund’s performance and provide a relevant basis of comparison to other real estate entities. In addition to IFRS results, these measures are also used internally to measure the operating performance of our property portfolio. These measures are not in accordance with IFRS and have no standardized definitions, as such, our computations of these non-IFRS measures may not be comparable to measures by other reporting issuers. In addition, Urbanfund’s method of calculating non-IFRS results may differ from other reporting issuers, and, accordingly, may not be comparable.

The Real Property Association of Canada (“REALpac”) issued a white paper in February 2019 prescribing revised definitions for certain non-IFRS financial measures of cash flow and operating performance commonly used by the Canadian real estate industry. Urbanfund has reviewed these guidelines and adopted certain measures, where appropriate, commencing with our fourth quarter 2017 reporting.

Funds From Operations (“FFO”)

Funds from Operations (“FFO”) is a non-IFRS financial measure of operating performance widely used by the Canadian real estate industry based on a white paper published in April 2014 and subsequently revised in February 2019. In the view of management, FFO better presents operating performance over IFRS net income and comprehensive income, which does not necessarily provide a complete view on performance. IFRS’s net income and comprehensive income includes items such as fair value adjustments on investment properties which are subject to market fluctuations, which is not representative of the Company’s year-over-year operating performance.

FFO is computed as IFRS consolidated net income and comprehensive income attributable to Urbanfund’s shareholders adjusted for items such as, but not limited to, fair value adjustments on investment properties, transaction gains and losses and fair market value adjustments on marketable securities. FFO should not be construed as an alternative to net income or cash flows provided by or used in operating activities as determined in accordance with IFRS. A reconciliation of FFO to IFRS net income is presented under the Results from Operations section above.

Adjusted Cash Flows from Operations (“ACFO”)

In February 2019, REALpac introduced a new non-IFRS measure called Adjusted Cash Flow from Operations (“ACFO”), which is intended to measure sustainable economic cash flow available for distributions. ACFO is used by management as an input, together with FFO to assess Urbanfund’s distribution payout ratios.

ACFO is computed as cash provided by or used in operating activities per IFRS plus, but not limited to adjustments for working capital items not considered to be indicative of sustainable economic cash flows for distributions, such as changes to other assets, indirect taxes payable and income taxes payable, cash distributions from investments, realized gains or losses from available-for-sale marketable securities and deducts capital expenditures. ACFO should not be construed as an alternative to cash flows provided by or used in operating activities as determined in accordance with IFRS. A reconciliation of ACFO to IFRS cash flow from or used in operating activities is presented under the Results from Operations section above.

Normalized Capital Expenditures

Normalized capital expenditures are an estimate made by management of the amount of ongoing capital investment required to maintain the condition of the physical property and the current rental revenues. Management will consider a number of items in estimating normalized capital expenditures given the age and size of the property portfolio, such as a review of historical capital expenditures and comparison of budgeted to actual on a quarterly basis.

Urbanfund does not obtain support from independent sources for normalized capital expenditures but relies on management’s expertise in arriving at this estimate. Both the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Executive Officer of the Company have extensive experience in residential and commercial real estate and in-depth knowledge of the property portfolio.

Actual capital expenditures can vary widely from quarter to quarter depending on a number of factors, management believes that normalized capital expenditures are a more relevant input than actual capital expenditures in assessing the Company’s ACFO and for determining appropriate levels of dividends over time. A number of factors affect variations in capital expenditures, including, lease expiries, tenant vacancies, age and location of the properties, and market conditions.

Net Operating Income (“NOI”)

NOI is a non-IFRS measure and is defined by Urbanfund as rental revenue from income properties less direct property costs such as utilities, property taxes adjusted to normalize the impact of the application requirements of IFRIC 21, Levies, repairs and maintenance, salaries, insurance, bad debt expenses, property management fees and other property specific costs. Management believes that NOI is a meaningful supplementary measure of the income generated from the Company’s income properties and is used in evaluating the portfolio, as well as a key input in determining the value of the income properties.

Adjusted Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization (“Adjusted EBITDA”)

Adjusted EBIDTA is a non-IFRS measure used by management as input in several of the debt metrics to measure Urbanfund’s debt profile in assessing the ability of the Company to satisfy obligations, including servicing of our debt. Adjusted EBITDA is used as an alternative to net income because it excludes major non-cash items such as fair value adjustments to investment properties and unrealized gains or losses on available-for-sale marketable securities, interest costs, current and deferred income tax expenses and recoveries, equity accounted investments and other items that management considers to be non-operating in nature. A reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to IFRS net income is presented under the Debt Profile of the MD&A.

Debt to Adjusted EBITDA

Debt to Adjusted EBITDA is a non-IFRS measure calculated on a trailing 12-month basis and is defined as quarterly average total debt (net of cash and cash equivalents) divided by Adjusted EBITDA as is calculated under the Debt Profile section of the MD&A.

Debt Service Ratio

Debt service ratio is a non-IFRS measure calculated on a trailing 12-month basis and is defined as Adjusted EBITDA divided by the sum of total interest costs (including interest costs capitalized) and scheduled mortgage principal repayments. It measures Urbanfund’s ability to meet debt obligations. Debt service ratio is calculated under the Debt Profile section of the MD&A.

Interest Coverage Ratio

Interest coverage ratio is a non-IFRS measure calculated on a trailing 12-month basis and is defined as Adjusted EBITDA divided by the sum of total interest costs (including interest costs capitalized) It measures Urbanfund’s ability to meet interest cost obligations. Interest coverage ratio is calculated under the Debt Profile section of the MD&A.

data.title: NTG Clarity Reports Q3 2026 Financial and Operating Results
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - NTG Clarity Networks Inc. (OTC Pink: NYWKF) ("NTG" or the "Company") today reported its financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. All figures are in Canadian dollars.

Q3 2026 Highlights

Comparisons are to the quarter ended September 30, 2025 unless otherwise stated.

  • Revenue: was $19.2M, down 7.9% year-over-year from $20.9M and down 4.3% from $20.1M in Q2 2026. The sequential decline has narrowed in each quarter of 2026 as the situation in the middle east shows early signs of stability. Year-to-date revenue is up approximately 2% year-over-year to $60.6M compared to $59.4M in 2025.

  • Gross Profit: was $6.3M or 33.0% of revenue, compared to $7.3M or 34.9%, reflecting pricing concessions on renewals.

  • Net Income: Total comprehensive income was $0.2M or 1.0% of revenue, compared to $1.9M or 9.1%, reflecting lower operating leverage in the quarter. NTG's delivery capacity is its strongest asset and keeping it in place, as discussed in Q2, allows us to take advantage of new opportunities.

  • Adjusted EBITDA: was $0.6M or 2.9% of revenue, compared to $2.5M or 11.9% in 2025, and compared to approximately nil in Q2 2026. Revenue was $0.9M lower than in Q2 2026 and the cost base was $1.4M lower.

  • Operating Cash Flow: of $3.2M, compared to an outflow of $3.3M in Q3 2025 and an outflow of $4.6M in Q2 2026. Cash was $3.4M at September 30, 2026, compared to $2.8M at June 30, 2026.

  • Purchase Orders: $33.4M announced in Q3 2026, or 1.7 times revenue, compared to $12.3M in Q2 2026

"We are seeing early signs of stability, both in the wider Saudi economy, where GDP recovered slightly from Q2, and in purchase order activity from our clients," said Adam Zaghloul, Vice President of Strategy & Planning at NTG Clarity. "Purchase orders were $33.4 million in the third quarter and we have announced a further $24.5 million since. Our focus now is staffing those orders and turning them into billings. Collections improved in the quarter, bringing receivables and unbilled contract assets down, and that progress has continued into the fourth quarter. We have worked with our clients on pricing and billing through a difficult period, and we believe that is how long-term relationships in the Kingdom are built."

Fiscal 2026 Financial Outlook

The prolonged conflict in the Middle East has disrupted oil shipments through the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea, on which many digitization initiatives in Saudi Arabia and the rest of the Gulf rely for funding. Saudi enterprises have responded with a focus on cost savings and return on investment. Some customers have negotiated more favourable pricing, paused expansion and in some cases scaled back their engagements.

Revenue declined again in Q3 as these adjustments took effect. However, order intake has been steadier, starting in Q3 and extending into the fourth quarter, with an increased pace of new purchase orders, a four-year extension of an existing framework agreement and a new three-year framework agreement with a new customer. NTG has worked with its customers through this period on pricing, on billing terms and on the size of their engagements. The Company believes that supporting its customers during these difficult conditions strengthens its standing in the region. The new framework agreement announced on November 17, 2026 marks the fourth portfolio company of one of the Kingdom's largest investment entities to become an NTG customer and is a sign of the growing position of NTG within some of the most prestigious companies in the region.

Management is continually evaluating the prospects for future growth against its delivery capacity with an eye towards cash generation and improving profitability. NTG's top priority is cash collections and receivables management so that it remains self-funded during the turbulence in the Middle East. Q3 showed progress, with an overall reduction in accounts receivable due to strong collections and no bad debts expected. Those collections continued into Q4, which showed receivables decreasing by approximately a further $4M by the end of October.

Conference Call Details

On Friday, November 27, 2026, at 9:00 AM ET, management will host a conference call webcast to discuss the Company's financial and operating results.

  • When: Friday, November 27, 2026, at 9:00 AM ET

data.title: BNB Chain details new layer-1 for trading, private finance and AI
data.description:
BNB Chain has outlined plans for a new layer-1 blockchain designed to support high-frequency trading, payments, private financial transactions and autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents.

According to a litepaper published Thursday, the network would operate alongside the existing BNB Smart Chain (BSC) and use BNB as its native token, with no new native token planned. The blockchain is currently running as a development network, with BNB Chain targeting a public testnet launch in the first quarter of 2027 and a mainnet launch in the second half of the year.

On general-purpose blockchains, applications typically compete for block space. The proposed network would reserve a portion of its transaction capacity for specific activities, such as payments services, which BNB Chain said could reduce competition for network resources during periods of high demand.

The proposed network would also feature an optional shielded pool designed to support private transfers involving BNB and other supported tokens, including certain decentralized finance (DeFi) transactions. Some transaction details would remain publicly visible, and BNB Chain’s documentation warns that the pool’s circuits remain unaudited and that it should not be used with real funds.

Other proposed features would allow users to transact without first acquiring BNB to pay network fees and authorize AI agents to execute transactions within predefined limits.

data.title: Binance restores withdrawals across nearly all networks four weeks after record $6.3B hack
data.description:
Binance says withdrawals are running again on nearly all of its supported networks. The restart comes roughly four weeks after attackers drained approximately $6.3 billion to $6.4 billion from the exchange's hot wallets, the largest crypto theft on record.

A small number of networks are still temporarily suspended. Binance says those pauses are for maintenance or planned upgrades unrelated to the hack.

The breach took place on October 29, 2026. Funds left the exchange across multiple blockchains in roughly 20 to 30 minutes, and Bitcoin and Ethereum took the heaviest hits.

Binance halted withdrawals quickly. It reopened them in stages, starting on November 1 with Bitcoin.

From there, the rollout widened network by network. By November 14, 2026, 87 networks were operational again, and most services were restored by late November.

Binance also sped up its proof-of-reserves process. Proof of reserves is a public accounting exercise meant to show that an exchange holds enough assets to cover customer deposits.

Binance pledged to make customers whole. The exchange committed over $6.34 billion to restore affected assets and set a target of completing reimbursement by November 12, 2026.

The money came from three sources: the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), the company's corporate treasury, and surplus from its futures insurance fund.

Binance has said no customer would bear losses from the incident.

Working with authorities, Binance helped freeze or intercept roughly $2.82 billion to $2.85 billion of the stolen assets, mostly stablecoins such as USDT and USDC.

The Department of Justice obtained court orders covering over $1.2 billion of the frozen funds. As of late November, though, only about $32 million had actually been recovered.

The attack has been attributed to TraderTraitor, a hacking group linked to North Korea. The attackers rapidly compromised Binance's internal systems, which let them withdraw across several chains at once.

data.title: Binance completes withdrawal recovery four weeks after $6.3B hack
data.description:
Binance said Thursday it had lifted all withdrawal suspensions related to its October hack, four weeks after an attack drained $6.3 billion in funds from the exchange in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.

In an announcement, Binance said withdrawals had resumed across nearly all networks, with a small number remaining temporarily suspended due to maintenance or planned upgrades unrelated to the hack.

The exchange’s network status page shows partial deposit and withdrawal suspensions for several cryptocurrencies. USDC withdrawals, for instance, remain suspended on Hedera and World Chain due to low hot wallet balances and on Sonic due to security issues.

Binance warned users against phishing attempts, saying it would never request passwords or seed phrases or offer expedited withdrawals. The exchange also said customers could verify that their assets are backed at a minimum ratio of 1:1 through its proof-of-reserves system.

The Oct. 29 attack targeted Binance’s hot wallets across multiple blockchains, with blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs attributing the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Following the breach, Binance said it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the losses.

Thursday’s announcement marks the end of a phased recovery process that began on Nov. 1, when Binance resumed Bitcoin withdrawals before gradually restoring services across other blockchain networks.
